clips.linkedin:
Give AI your strategy and this quarter's campaign briefs, and it shows which campaigns serve no line of it.

This clip is about what happens after a campaign disappoints. If you only measure results, a strong idea delivered a week late looks exactly like a weak idea, and the team learns the wrong lesson.

So measure execution on its own terms. On time, on brief, free of errors. Then walk back up the chain. Execution first, because it's cheapest to fix, then creative, then the campaign, and question the strategy last.

AI can do a lot of that walking. Give it the campaign plan, the delivery log and the results, and it sorts what went wrong into those four, with the evidence for each.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/strategy-campaign-creative-execution-basics/
clips.text: You were quite firm in the article about measuring execution separately. Because otherwise you learn the wrong lesson. If you only measure results, a strong idea delivered a week late looks exactly like a weak idea. So measure execution on its own terms. On time, on brief, free of errors. Which brings us to the bit that ties it together. Every layer should trace back to the one above it. Every piece of execution delivers part of a creative idea, every creative idea serves a campaign objective, and every campaign carries part of the strategy. When a result disappoints, walk back up the chain in that order. Execution first, because it's cheapest to fix. Then creative. Then the campaign. And question the strategy last.

clips.linkedin:
Give AI your strategy and this quarter's campaign briefs, and it shows which campaigns serve no line of it.

The quick test for any campaign is whether its brief names the line of the strategy it serves. If it can't, either the campaign shouldn't run or the strategy has a gap. It kills a lot of pet projects.

Write your strategy in a couple of sentences and hand it over with the briefs. What comes back is a table showing which line each campaign serves, which briefs connect to nothing, and which audiences are too vague to brief creative against.

The second job is for when a campaign disappoints. It sorts the problem into execution, creative, campaign or strategy, and tells you where the data is too thin to say.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. The prompts, full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/strategy-campaign-creative-execution-basics/
clips.text: Get AI on this: checking every campaign brief traces back to the strategy. Give it your strategy, written in a couple of sentences, and this quarter's campaign briefs. It hands back a table showing which line of the strategy each campaign serves, which briefs don't connect to any line, and which audiences are too vague to brief creative against. Second, get AI on separating execution problems from idea problems when a campaign disappoints. Give it the campaign plan, the delivery log with what went live when, and the results. It sorts what went wrong into execution, creative, campaign and strategy, with the evidence for each, and tells you where the data's too thin to say.
